rationale: Retaining the combine interceptor until page teardown prevents the last one-shot handler from being removed at the moment the application issues recovery GET. It still commits the injected action only in committed scenarios and aborts the first browser response exactly once. Subsequent requests are continued rather than silently swallowed and now fail the explicit one-request count if the application replays a mutation. The GET is real and its authoritative inventory remains the basis of every existing focus and discovery assertion. This is a narrow harness repair rather than a change to application behavior or success criteria. The two-case extension applies that same behavior to the remaining earlier empty-reply recovery tests after a matching pending-GET failure. It preserves committed/uncommitted authoritative empty-pair truth and partner styling, while making duplicate client mutation or recovery reads explicit failures.
